questions.question: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">In order to jump off the floor, the floor must exert a force on you<\/div>$\n$
options: In the direction of and equal to your weight.
Opposite to and equal to your weight
Opposite to and less than your weight.
Opposite to and greater than your weight.
questions.explanation:
**QUESTION EXPLANATION
$ The$ question asks what kind of force the floor must exert on a person for them to be able to jump upwards.
$ $
$ $**CONCEPT
$ To$ achieve a net upward acceleration (a requirement to jump), the upward force from the floor must be greater than the downward force of the person's weight. This is a direct application of Newton's Second Law (Fnet$\u$200b = ma).
$ $
$ $**SOLUTION
$ To$ jump force has to be larger than weight.
$ $
$ $**CORRECT ANSWER
$ The$ correct option is **(4) Opposite to and greater than your weight.
$ $
